components.note: 亻 (person) — one person giving to another
共 (gòng) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone, and its two hands match the idea of offering

example.english: The school provides housing for students.
example.fact: 供 is read gōng for 'supply' (提供, 供应, 供电) and gòng for 'offer, confess': 供品 (offerings), 供认 (to confess). Pay attention to the tone, since the two readings are different words.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — an action done by hand, such as marking or striking
比 (bǐ) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.english: This batch of goods will arrive tomorrow.
example.fact: 批 works as a measure word for batches (一批货, 第一批). It also builds 批准 (to approve), 批评 (to criticize), 批发 (wholesale) and 批改 (to mark homework).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pushing and squeezing by hand
齐 (qí) gives a loose sound hint — shared -i ending, different tone

example.pinyin: Dìtiě lǐ jǐ mǎn le rén.
example.english: The subway was packed with people.
example.fact: 挤 describes both squeezing in and being crowded: 太挤了 (so crowded), 拥挤 (crowded), 挤地铁 (to cram into the subway). 挤牙膏 is also literally to squeeze out toothpaste, and figuratively to reveal something bit by bit.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — picking up by hand
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ian ending

example.hanzi: 他在路上捡到一个钱包。
example.pinyin: Tā zài lù shàng jiǎn dào yí gè qiánbāo.
example.english: He found a wallet on the road.
example.fact: 捡 is the casual verb for picking something up from the ground, especially finding things by luck: 捡到 (come across), 捡垃圾 (pick up trash). 捡漏 is slang for getting a bargain by luck. 拾 is a more formal alternative.

components.note: 纟 (silk) — in the old sense, cloth absorbing or taking in
内 (nèi) gives a loose sound hint — the same vowel; it also means 'inside'

example.hanzi: 这个房间能容纳一百个人。
example.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān néng róngnà yìbǎi gè rén.
example.english: This room can hold a hundred people.
example.fact: 纳 is formal and shows up in compounds: 接纳 (to accept), 容纳 (to hold), 纳税 (to pay taxes), 出纳 (cashier) and 纳闷 (to feel puzzled).

components.note: 灬 (fire) — cooking food through
孰 (shú) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.english: This apple isn't ripe yet.
example.fact: 熟 covers ripe, cooked and familiar: 煮熟 (cook thoroughly), 成熟 (mature), 熟人 (acquaintance), 熟悉 (be familiar with). Conversationally it is often read shóu, as in 饭熟了.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — the upper part; explanations of its role differ
口 (mouth) — speech

example.pinyin: Wǒ gàosu nǐ yí gè hǎo xiāoxi.
example.english: I have good news to tell you.
example.fact: 告 forms 告诉 (to tell), 报告 (report), 广告 (advertisement), 告别 (to say farewell) and 告状 (to tell on someone). In the legal sense it also means to sue.

components.note: 木 (wood) — the old word referred to a wooden label or slip used for sealing
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ian ending

example.pinyin: Yīshēng yào gěi nǐ zuò jiǎnchá.
example.english: The doctor is going to give you an examination.
example.fact: 检 appears in 检查 (to inspect, to check), 体检 (physical exam), 检验 (to test) and 检讨 (self-criticism). 检查 can be anything from a quick check to a medical examination.

components.note: Often read as a hand lifting a ladle, the same cup that gives the 'liter' sense; details of the old form are uncertain.

example.english: The sun rises in the east.
example.fact: 升 means to rise and is the same character used for 'liter' (一升水). It builds 升级 (to upgrade), 升职 (to be promoted) and 升旗 (to raise a flag). The opposite is 降 (jiàng).

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun is gone, so it is dark
音 (yīn) gives a loose sound hint — shared -in/-an ending

example.english: It is very dark in the room.
example.fact: 暗 is dark in the sense of dim light: 黑暗 (darkness), 昏暗 (gloomy). It also means hidden or secret: 暗示 (to hint), 暗恋 (to have a secret crush). 黑 (hēi) is more about color black.

components.note: 广 (shed) — a building
车 (cart) — the old storehouse held chariots and weapons

example.pinyin: Huòwù dōu fàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
example.english: The goods are all kept in the warehouse.
example.fact: 库 is a store for things: 仓库 (warehouse), 车库 (garage), 水库 (reservoir), 库存 (inventory). It also names digital storage, as in 数据库 (database) and 题库 (question bank).

components.note: 丘 — the top part, which stands for an axe-like weapon, not a hill
八 — two hands holding the weapon

example.english: He serves as a soldier in the army.
example.fact: 兵 means soldier: 当兵 (join the army), 士兵 (soldier), 骑兵 (cavalry). 兵马俑 is the name of the Terracotta Army figurines, and 纸上谈兵 is an idiom about 'discussing war only on paper'.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — a cutting action
害 (hài) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā yòng dāo gēkāi le shéngzi.
example.english: He cut the rope with a knife.
example.fact: 割 is cutting with a sweeping stroke, such as reaping or slicing: 收割 (harvest), 割草 (mow grass). 割舍 means to give up something dear, and 割肉 is also stock-market slang for selling at a loss.

components.note: Old forms show a hand with bent fingers; the 'ugly' meaning came by merging with 醜 in simplification, so the shape does not hint at it.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo yāzi hěn chǒu.
example.english: This little duckling is very ugly.
example.fact: 丑 is the opposite of 美, and the simplified form also stands for the old character 醜. In Chinese opera 丑 is the clown role, and 丑 is the second of the twelve Earthly Branches, linked to the Ox. 丑闻 means scandal.

components.note: 並 (side by side) — everyone together
日 (sun) — everywhere the sun shines

example.english: He can speak Mandarin.
example.fact: 普 means widespread: 普通话 (Mandarin, literally 'common speech'), 普通 (ordinary), 普遍 (universal), 普及 (to popularize). It is the 'general' in 普通 and rarely stands alone.

components.note: 木 (tree) — three trees stacked together make a dense forest

example.english: It is very quiet in the forest.
example.fact: 木, 林 and 森 show one, two and three trees, a neat example of repeating a character to show 'more'. 森 appears in 森林 (forest) and 阴森 (eerie). It is also a surname and part of many given names.

components.note: The old form shows a person climbing a tree; the modern parts 禾 and 北 are a distorted version of that picture.

example.english: We're taking a plane to Shanghai.
example.fact: 乘 is a formal 'ride', as in 乘车 (ride a vehicle), 乘客 (passenger) and 乘坐. It is also 'multiply': 三乘四等于十二, and 乘法 is multiplication.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — an enclosure
牛 (ox) — livestock kept in the pen

example.pinyin: Tā zài láo lǐ dāi le sān nián.
example.english: He spent three years in prison.
example.fact: 牢 began as a pen for livestock, as the idiom 亡羊补牢 ('mend the pen after the sheep are lost') shows. It became 'prison' (坐牢) and 'firm' (牢固, 牢记 'remember firmly'). 牢骚 means grumbling.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the palm is part of the hand
尚 (shàng) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ang ending

example.english: His palm is very big.
example.fact: 掌 builds 手掌 (palm), 鼓掌 (to applaud), 掌声 (applause) and 掌握 (to master, grasp). It also means to hold power: 掌权.

components.note: 足 (foot) — squatting is a foot and leg posture
尊 (zūn) gives a loose sound hint — same vowel and ending, different tone

example.pinyin: Tā dūn zài dì shàng kàn mǎyǐ.
example.english: He is squatting on the ground watching ants.
example.fact: 蹲 is to squat: 蹲下 (squat down), 蹲厕 (squat toilet). It extends to staying in one place for a long time, as in 蹲点 (to be stationed at a spot) and 蹲守 (to stake out).

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — cloth being made into a garment
刀 (knife) — cutting the cloth, the first step in making clothes

example.english: We are meeting for the first time.
example.fact: 初 means the start of something: 初次 (first time), 初中 (junior high), 月初 (beginning of the month), 初恋 (first love). 初一 is the first day of a lunar month; 大年初一 is Chinese New Year's Day.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquid drops
啇 (dí) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.english: The faucet is dripping.
example.fact: 滴 is both a verb (to drip) and a measure word for drops: 一滴水 (a drop of water). 点滴 means 'bit by bit', and in China 打点滴 is the common way to say getting an IV drip.

components.note: 戈 (spear) — a weapon
廾 (two hands) — hands holding the weapon, on guard

example.english: He decided to quit smoking.
example.fact: 戒 means to give up a habit: 戒烟 (quit smoking), 戒酒 (stop drinking). It also appears in 戒指 (a finger ring), 警戒 (to be on alert) and 戒备 (to guard against).

components.note: 礻 (spirit, altar) — rites and offerings
乚 stands in for the sound part of the traditional 禮 — only a rough fit

example.hanzi: 他送了我一份生日礼物。
example.pinyin: Tā sòng le wǒ yí fèn shēngrì lǐwù.
example.english: He gave me a birthday present.
example.fact: 礼 is one of the core Confucian ideas, covering ritual and etiquette. In daily life it builds 礼貌 (politeness), 礼物 (gift), 婚礼 (wedding) and 礼拜 (week, or a religious service).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — spurting out, like from the mouth
贲 (bēn) gives a loose sound hint — close, differing in tone

example.english: He sprayed on a little perfume.
example.fact: 喷 is to spray or spurt out: 喷水 (spray water), 喷泉 (fountain), 喷漆 (to spray-paint), 打喷嚏 (to sneeze). On the internet, 喷子 is slang for a person who criticizes in an aggressive way.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — throwing is done with the hand
The right-hand part gives the sound pāo; its inner pieces have no clear separate meaning today.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ qiú pāo gěi wǒ.
example.english: He tossed the ball to me.
example.fact: 抛 is to throw upward or away: 抛球 (toss a ball), 抛弃 (abandon). 车抛锚了 literally 'the car dropped its anchor' means the car broke down, and 抛头露面 means to appear in public.

components.note: A foot, shown as toes on the ground; a foot that stays put gives the idea 'stop'.

example.english: Please stop talking.
example.fact: 止 was originally a drawing of a foot, and it survives in characters like 步 (step) and 走 (walk). It later meant 'stop': 停止, 禁止 (to prohibit) and 制止 (to put a stop to). 禁止吸烟 is the 'no smoking' sign.

components.note: 冖 (cover) — an encirclement or camp
车 (chariot) — chariots drawn up around a camp

example.pinyin: Tā zài jūnduì gōngzuò le shí nián.
example.english: He worked in the army for ten years.
example.fact: 军 is the root of military words: 军人 (soldier), 军队 (army), 海军 (navy), 空军 (air force), 将军 (general). The old form is often explained as chariots encircling a camp.

components.note: 戈 (spear) — a cutting tool
刂 (knife) — another cutting tool; together they show cutting a line

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ huà yì tiáo xiàn.
example.english: Please draw a line here.
example.fact: 划 is read huà in 计划 (plan), 规划 (planning) and 划分 (to divide). The reading huá is for paddling and scratching: 划船 (row a boat), 划算 (to be worth it), 划伤 (to scratch).

components.note: 山 (mountain) — a dense, thick mountain thicket
宓 (mì) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.english: The trees here are very dense.
example.fact: 密 is thick and close: 密度 (density), 亲密 (close, intimate), 密切 (close, closely linked). It is also secret: 秘密, 密码 (password), 保密 (to keep secret).

components.note: Commonly read as two people close together; the word first meant a person's facial expression and then broadened to color.

example.english: What color do you like?
example.fact: 色 forms colors (红色, 黄色) and 颜色 (color). It can also mean expression (脸色) or lust (好色). In casual speech 色 is read shǎi, as in 掉色 (to fade) and 色子 (dice).

components.note: 音 (sound) — music
十 (ten) — the old explanation is ten parts, a full musical piece

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yígòng yǒu shí'èr zhāng.
example.english: This book has twelve chapters in total.
example.fact: 章 is the measure word for chapters (第一章) and also means a seal or stamp: 盖章 (to stamp with a seal) is a daily act in Chinese offices. It builds 文章 (article), 勋章 (medal) and 规章 (regulations).

components.note: 女 (woman) — a girl
丑 (chǒu) gives a loose sound hint — shared vowel is not close

example.pinyin: Tā jiào Niūniu, jīnnián sān suì.
example.english: Her name is Niuniu and she is three years old.
example.fact: 妞 is a colloquial northern word for girl, as in Beijing's 小妞儿. 妞妞 is a common nickname for baby girls. Used for adult women, it can sound flirty or patronizing, so tone and context matter.

excludeSuggestion: Regional colloquial term for 'girl', rarely used in neutral or formal speech.

components.note: 彡 (streaks) — light and shade strokes
景 (jǐng) gives the sound — close, and it once meant sunlight, from which the shadow forms

example.english: Let's go and see a movie.
example.fact: 影 means shadow or image. 电影 (movie) is literally 'electric shadow'. It also builds 影子 (shadow), 影响 (influence), 摄影 (photography) and 影院 (cinema).

components.note: 讠 (speech) — poetry is spoken words
寺 (sì) gives a loose sound hint — the vowel is close

example.english: He likes to read Tang poetry.
example.fact: 诗 counts with the measure word 首 (一首诗). The Tang dynasty is considered the golden age of Chinese poetry, with poets like 李白 and 杜甫. The oldest poetry collection is the 诗经, the Book of Songs.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a plum tree
子 (zǐ) gives a loose sound hint — the vowel is similar, the initial differs

example.english: This plum is very sweet.
example.fact: 李 is the plum (李子) and also one of the most common surnames in the world, the Li of 李白 and 李小龙 (Bruce Lee). 行李 (luggage) also contains it, though that is an unrelated compound.

components.note: The picture is a ladle or dipper, as in the older word 斗 (dǒu); the 'fight' sense comes from the character 鬥, which merged into 斗 in simplification.

example.hanzi: 我们晚上一起斗地主吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang yìqǐ dòu dìzhǔ ba.
example.english: Let's play Dou Dizhu together tonight.
example.fact: 斗 is read dòu for fighting and competing, from the old 鬥: 斗争 (struggle), 战斗 (battle), 斗地主 (a popular card game, 'fight the landlord'). Read dǒu, it is a ladle or measure, as in 北斗 (the Big Dipper).

components.note: 卜 (divination crack) — an oracle sign
口 (mouth) — asking or announcing what the oracle says

example.hanzi: 这张桌子占了很多地方。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi zhàn le hěn duō dìfang.
example.english: This table takes up a lot of space.
example.fact: 占 is zhàn for occupying and for proportions: 占线 (line busy), 占座 (reserve a seat), 占 20% (account for). Read zhān, it means to divine, as in 占卜 (fortune-telling).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and calling come from the mouth
乎 (hū) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.english: Please take a deep breath.
example.fact: 呼 is exhaling, and 吸 is inhaling, together 呼吸 (breathing). 呼 also means to call out: 招呼 (to greet; 打招呼 means to say hello) and 称呼 (a form of address).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken pronoun
自 (zì) gives a loose sound hint — a rough match

example.english: Let's go together.
example.fact: 咱们 is the inclusive 'we', which always includes the listener, unlike 我们, which may leave them out. It is typical of northern and Beijing speech and sounds friendly and close.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a sound made with the mouth
矣 (yǐ) gives a loose sound hint — the vowel is close

example.english: Sigh, I have to work overtime again today.
example.fact: 唉 is a sigh of regret or resignation, often drawn out. 唉声叹气 is the idiom for sighing in distress. It can also be a quick reply meaning 'yes'. A rising or falling tone changes the mood.

components.note: The picture is debated; a common reading is an axe, fitting the early warrior-official class.

example.english: She is a nurse.
example.fact: 士 was the lowest rank of ancient nobility, then the scholar class, the first of the 士农工商 (scholar, farmer, artisan, merchant). Today it ends job and title words: 护士 (nurse), 博士 (doctorate), 战士 (soldier), 女士 (Ms.).

components.note: 阝 (mound) — an earth wall, a defensive barrier
方 (fāng) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.english: In summer you need sun protection when going out.
example.fact: 防 means to guard against: 预防 (to prevent), 防止 (to prevent), 防火 (fire prevention), 国防 (national defense). Product words use it too: 防水 (waterproof) and 防晒 (sunscreen).

components.note: 里 (village, land) — countryside
予 (yǔ) gives a loose sound hint — shared vowel quality is distant

example.hanzi: 森林里有很多野生动物。
example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu hěn duō yěshēng dòngwù.
example.english: There are many wild animals in the forest.
example.fact: 野 describes the wild or outdoors: 野生 (wild-growing), 野外 (outdoors), 野餐 (picnic), 田野 (fields). 野心 means ambition, sometimes with a negative edge. As an adjective it can also mean rough and untamed.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a hero is a person
夹 (jiā) gives a loose sound hint — the ending is the same

example.english: I like reading martial arts novels.
example.fact: 侠 is the wandering hero who upholds justice. The 武侠 (wuxia) genre, popularized by authors like 金庸 (Jin Yong), is built on this ideal. 大侠 is a great hero, and 侠义 means chivalry.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a body of water
胡 (hú) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Hú lǐ yǒu hěn duō yú.
example.english: There are many fish in the lake.
example.fact: 湖 names many famous lakes, like 西湖 in Hangzhou. The provinces 湖南 and 湖北 mean 'south of the lake' and 'north of the lake', after Dongting Lake. 江湖, 'rivers and lakes', is the wandering outsider world of wuxia stories.

components.note: A fishing net with crossing strings, shown as a frame filled with cross-hatching.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shàng mǎi le yì běn shū.
example.english: I bought a book online.
example.fact: 网 is a net, and in modern Chinese it means the internet: 上网 (go online), 网站 (website), 网购 (shop online), 网红 (internet celebrity). 网 is also a fishing net: 渔网.

components.note: 土 (earth) — building up soil or bricks
厽 (lěi) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.hanzi: 他们用石头垒了一道墙。
example.pinyin: Tāmen yòng shítou lěi le yí dào qiáng.
example.english: They built a wall out of stones.
example.fact: 垒 is to stack up stones or bricks: 垒墙 (build a wall). It builds 堡垒 (fortress) and baseball terms: 垒球 (softball), 一垒 (first base), 全垒打 (home run).

components.note: 石 (stone) — bowls were originally ceramic or stone
宛 (wǎn) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì wǎn mǐfàn.
example.english: Please give me a bowl of rice.
example.fact: 碗 is both a bowl and a measure word (一碗饭). 饭碗, a rice bowl, also means one's livelihood: 铁饭碗 ('iron rice bowl') is a secure job, once typically a state job.

components.note: ⺈ (a person) — the figure at the top
贝 (shell, money) — a person carrying valuables on the back

example.english: He has to be responsible for this project.
example.fact: 负 builds 负责 (to be responsible), 负担 (burden), 负债 (to owe debt) and 负数 (negative number). 胜负 means win or lose, and 负 is the 'lost' side in a score. It is the opposite of 正 in many contexts.
